title: The Concept of the Other and Intersubjectivity
text:
In sociological theory, 'the Other' refers to a concept used to delineate group boundaries. It represents any external entity—a culture, a marginalized group, or even an abstract ideal—that is perceived as fundamentally different from the self or ingroup. This dynamic of defining difference is crucial for understanding social identity formation and power structures.

Intersubjectivity suggests that shared reality does not exist purely within individual minds but emerges through mutual recognition between consciousnesses. It implies a foundational psychological agreement necessary for cooperative living, where individuals navigate meaning by acknowledging the perspective of others.
